summary: This paper advances the theory of constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes by resolving Open Problems 1 and 2 posed by Liu et al. (arXiv:2611.34386v1). It provides a universal O(1) closed-form evaluation for the hypergraph penalty zw-1(x) eliminating Frobenius number restrictions, introduces two dual gap-closing optimal BIBD/RBIBD families, establishes an even-t residual-degree jump and exact h3-attaining transversal-design theorem with an r = 2 non-existence dichotomy, and constructs explicit finite affine-plane optimal codes. All results are fully formalized in Lean 4.36.0 and validated with zero-float Python suites.
strengths: Complete formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry, zero grind, and zero custom axioms across 20 core theorems.
Elimination of Frobenius-number restrictions via universal O(1) closed-form evaluation of zw-1(x).
Introduction of Dual Family A and Dual Family B successfully covering Liu et al.'s open gap.
Exhaustive AST-pure zero-float verification and cryptographic SHA-256 manifest.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on asymptotic existence theorems (Wilson, Chang) for infinite families, though mitigated by explicit finite constructions such as AG(2, p) and TD(q+1, q).
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal O(1) Closed-Form Theorem for zw-1(x) eliminating Diophantine Frobenius number machinery.
Dual Gap-Closing Optimal BIBD/RBIBD Families A and B covering the open gap w-3 <= t < (w-3)floor((w-2)/3)-1.
Even-t residual-degree threshold and exact h3-attaining transversal-design family with r = 2 non-existence dichotomy.
